issues.legal_issue: A memorandum concerning a mortgage created by depositing title deeds requires registration only if the parties intended it to embody and operate as their agreement creating the security.
material_facts: The debtor deposited title deeds with the creditor as security for amounts already due and amounts that might become due from their business dealings.
After the deposit, the debtor signed and delivered a memorandum stating that the deeds had been deposited with intent to create an equitable mortgage.

The courts found that the parties had already agreed orally on the security and that the memorandum merely recorded the completed transaction; it was not intended to form the basis of their rights and liabilities.
issues.conclusion: The memorandum did not require registration and was admissible in evidence to prove creation of the charge. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a mortgage may arise when title deeds are delivered with the requisite intention to create security. Ordinarily, the contract is implied by law from the deposit and intention. If the parties instead reduce their bargain to an operative written agreement, that document creates an interest in immovable property and requires registration under section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908; section 59 addresses registration of other forms of mortgage. If the document merely records a transaction already concluded and is evidential rather than operative, it does not require registration. The timing of the memorandum is not decisive. Obla Sundarachariar v. Narayana Ayyar illustrates an evidential memorandum that did not require registration; Hari Sankar Paul v. Kedar Nath Saha illustrates an operative written agreement that did.

rule.if: title_deed_security_dispute and bargain_completed_on_deposit and not memorandum_as_operating_agreement

predicates.title_deed_security_dispute: The dispute concerns whether a memorandum connected with security created by depositing title deeds must be registered.
predicates.bargain_completed_on_deposit: The debtor deposited title deeds with the creditor with the requisite intention to secure the debt, and the security bargain was already concluded at that time.
predicates.memorandum_as_operating_agreement: The debtor and creditor intended the memorandum itself to embody their agreement and operate as the instrument creating the security.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns security created by depositing title deeds and the security bargain was already concluded on deposit, a memorandum not intended to operate as the agreement creating the security is admissible without registration.
